'''Tim Ohlbrecht''' (born August 30, 1988) is a German former professional [[basketball]] player. He won 84 caps for the German men's national team, competing in the 2008 Olympic Games, the 2010 World Championships as well as the European Championships in 2009 and 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Spiele von Tim Ohlbrecht (84)|url=https://mahr.sb-vision.de/dbb/html/herren/spieler/spielespieler.aspx?spnr=184|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-12-02|website=mahr.sb-vision.de}}</ref> He mostly played for teams in the German Bundesliga. Ohlbrecht had three NBA appearances for the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tim Ohlbrecht Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/ohlbrti01.html|access-date=2020-12-02|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> He won two [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]] championships.

==Professional career==
Ohlbrecht began his professional playing career with the [[Basketball Bundesliga|German League]] club [[Bayer Giants Leverkusen]], during the 2005–06 season. He then signed with the German League club [[Brose Baskets]] in 2006. He was [[sports loan|loaned]] to TSV Breitengüßbach, where he played in both the [[2. Basketball Bundesliga|German 2nd Division]], and the German 3rd Division, from 2006 to 2008. He was also loaned to [[Nürnberger BC]], where he played in the German 2nd Division, during the 2007–08 season.

Ohlbrecht, due to his age, was available for the [[2010 NBA draft]],<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.nba.com/draft2010/prospects/tim-ohlbrecht/|title=Prospect profile: Tim Ohlbrecht|website=[[NBA.com]] |accessdate=January 29, 2015}}</ref> but subsequently went [[undrafted]]. Ohlbrecht then signed with [[Telekom Baskets Bonn]] for the 2010–11 season. In the summer of 2011, he signed with [[Skyliners Frankfurt]] for the 2011–12 season.

In November 2012, Ohlbrecht was acquired by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]]. On February 4, 2013, he was named to the Prospects All-Star team for the 2013 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html|title=2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced|work=[[National 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Rockets sent Ohlbrecht back to the Vipers as a D-League assignee on April 9, 2013.<ref>{{cite news|accessdate=April 10, 2013|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/rockets_assign_ohlbrecht_2013_04_09.html|title=Houston Rockets Assign Tim Ohlbrecht to NBA D-League Affiliate Rio Grande Valley Vipers|date=April 9, 2013|archivedate=March 28, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140328063621/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/rockets_assign_ohlbrecht_2013_04_09.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On July 15, 2013, he was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite news|publisher=[[Inside Hoops]]|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13779|title=Houston Rockets waive James Anderson and Tim Ohlbrecht, and announce signings|accessdate=July 16, 2013|archivedate=November 15, 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131115014555/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13779|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 16, 2013, he was claimed off of waivers by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13793|title=Philadelphia 76ers claim James Anderson and Tim Ohlbrecht off waivers|publisher=Inside Hoops|accessdate=July 17, 2013|archivedate=November 15, 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131115014828/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13793|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the 76ers on October 16.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14557|title=Sixers sign Daniel Orton, waive Tim Ohlbrecht|publisher=Inside Hoops|accessdate=October 16, 2013|archivedate=October 17, 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017083810/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14557|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On November 30, 2013, he was re-acquired by the Rio Grande Valley Vipers.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2013/11/30/5160146/tim-ohlbrecht-returns-to-nba-d-league-with-rio-grande-valley-vipers|author=Keith Schlosser|title=Tim Ohlbrecht Returns to NBA D-League With Rio Grande Valley Vipers|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|work=Ridiculous Upside|date=November 30, 2013|accessdate=December 1, 2013|archivedate=December 3, 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203053403/http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2013/11/30/5160146/tim-ohlbrecht-returns-to-nba-d-league-with-rio-grande-valley-vipers|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 1, 2014, he was traded to the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/VipersTradeTimOhlbrecht030114.html|title=Vipers trade Tim Ohlbrecht|work=NBA.com|date=March 1, 2014|accessdate=March 4, 2014|archivedate=June 1, 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140601005003/http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/VipersTradeTimOhlbrecht030114.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 5, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with [[ratiopharm Ulm]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Tim Ohlbrecht signs with Ratiopharm Ulm|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/130316/tim-ohlbrecht-signs-with-ratiopharm-ulm.html|accessdate=5 August 2014|work=Sportando.com}}</ref>

On July 27, 2015, he signed with the Russian club [[BC Yenisey Krasnoyarsk|Yenisey Krasnoyarsk]] for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tim Ohlbrecht signs with Enisey Krasnoyarsk|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/170620/tim-ohlbrecht-signs-with-enisey-krasnoyarsk.html|accessdate=27 July 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=27 July 2015}}</ref>

On June 30, 2016, Ohlbrecht returned to ratiopharm Ulm, signing a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ratiopharm Ulm signs Tim Ohlbrecht to a two-year contract|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/204208/ratiopharm-ulm-signs-tim-ohlbrecht-to-a-two-year-contract.html|accessdate=30 June 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=30 June 2016}}</ref> On May 6, 2017, he signed a contract extension with Ulm till June 2020.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ratiopharm Ulm signs Tim Ohlbrecht to a contract extension till 2020|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/233891/ratiopharm-ulm-signs-tim-ohlbrecht-to-a-contract-extension-till-2020.html|accessdate=May 13, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=May 6, 2017}}</ref>

He retired in 2018 due to problems with his knees.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Boerne, TX March 2020|url=https://issuu.com/lifestylepubs/docs/https___s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com__6e9fc02004736e|access-date=2020-12-02|website=Issuu|date=February 13, 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

==German national team==
Ohlbrecht made his debut with the senior men's [[Germany national basketball team|German national basketball team]] in 2008. He participated, together with [[Dirk Nowitzki]], in the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]]. Ohlbrecht played again for Germany at the [[EuroBasket 2009]], the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], and the [[EuroBasket 2011]].

== After his career ==
Ohlbrecht settled in [[Boerne, Texas]] and became a [[realtor]].<ref name=":0" /> He also founded the Tim Ohlbrecht Elite Basketball program, offering individual practice for youth and collegiate athletes as well as basketball camps for children.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tim Ohlbrecht Elite Basketball - Youth Training and Coaching|url=https://www.to-elitebasketball.com/about-tim-ohlbrecht-elite-basketbal|access-date=2020-12-02|website=Elite Basketball|language=en}}</ref>
